title: Semiparametric Efficiency for Multi-Source Transport with Source-Specific Confounders
banked_reason: D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 7.3 < 7.4, so the graded tier field is capped at subfield; no bounded in-scope fix.
gap_reasons: The asserted R_n=o_P(n^{-1/2}) and weighted fitted-nuisance convergences are estimator-side conclusions with no primitive learner/rate conditions or achievability argument; discharge them from stated nuisance rates (including support leakage) or state the theorem only for a named regime where they hold.

Attainment is conditional on a high-level weighted remainder that includes fitted-support and off-target coefficient leakage, without concrete learner or tuning constructions that verify these conditions in the continuous-covariate setting.

The semaglutide analysis remains only a proposed consumer, with no reanalysis or numerical study demonstrating the magnitude of the efficiency gain or the practical incidence of the infinite-bound branch.
proof_attempt_summary: The D-stage note derived a measurable exact-path construction, constrained tangent space, inverse-information canonical gradient, and finite-versus-infinite information branch. Its attainment theorem is conditional on weighted nuisance and leakage rates; the final math review requested a concrete learner regime establishing those rates. D0.5.G capped the delivered package at subfield (7.3 below the field threshold of 7.4), and an independent validity check found no false mathematical claim or bounded in-scope path to the field floor.
tldr: Multiple source studies may require different confounder sets and may observe outcomes under different missing-at-random mechanisms. Under Su et al.'s joint source overlap, equality is imposed only across sources active at a target covariate value. A measurable reference-source calibration proves the full active-source tangent space; its projection yields the globally canonical inverse-conditional-variance gradient, the exact finite-versus-infinite information boundary, and a cross-fitted one-step estimator that attains the finite bound under explicit weighted nuisance products and fitted-support leakage control.
gap: Su et al. explicitly leave the semiparametric efficiency bound open when studies adjust for different confounders, because equality applies to means of source-specific adjusted contrasts and their tangent construction no longer applies. Their relative-efficiency result does not certify global canonicality, and it does not model regional outcome dropout.
fill: An exact equality-preserving conditional-kernel path will establish tangent maximality. Projection then yields inverse-conditional-variance source weights, an exact finite-information criterion, an infinite-bound converse, and an efficient cross-fitted estimator under transparent weighted nuisance products.
